gallery.filename: NLS Haig - Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead.jpg
gallery.title: File:NLS Haig - Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead.jpg
gallery.credit: This image is available from the National Library of Scotland under the sequence number or Shelfmark ID D.1520. You can see this image in its original context, along with the rest of the Library's digital collections, under digital.nls.uk/74547058 in the NLS Digital Gallery
gallery.source: NLS Haig - Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead
gallery.description: This is a disturbing image of a destroyed German trench. In the foreground the limp bodies of dead German soldiers lie amidst the rubble. It is difficult to distinguish the soldiers from the chaos around them, but four bodies are clearly visible. One man, wearing a helmet, has been pushed forward by the blast and, although dead, appears to crouch forward. The entire scene is a maelstrom of mud, splintered wood and dead bodies.Original reads: 'OFFICIAL PHOTOGRAPHS TAKEN ON THE BRITISH WESTERN FRONT. Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead.'Photographs from the Haig "Official Photographs" series
categories: Black and white photographs of corpses
Bodies of dead soldiers in World War I
German casualties of World War I

gallery.filename: Irish Peace Park, Messines 1917 Battle plaque.jpg
gallery.title: File:Irish Peace Park, Messines 1917 Battle plaque.jpg
gallery.source: Irish Peace Park, Messines 1917 Battle plaque
gallery.description: An elevated bronze plaque showing the direction of assault at the outset of the Battle of Messines in June 1917 in which the two voluntary Irish divisions, the 36th (Ulster) Division and the 16th (Irish) Division, played a decisive role. The plaque stands in the grounds of the Island of Ireland Peace Park, Messines, Belgium.
